newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - July 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - July 1.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

British telecommunications company Cable & Wireless has been confirmed as the new major shareholder in Australian telecommunications company Optus Communications, whose board approved the acquisition yesterday. Cable & Wireless has struck a deal with US company Bell South to buy its 24.5 per cent stake in Optus for approximately A$1 billion. Page 25.

General Motors Holden's Automotive Ltd has retained its position as Australia's leading car manufacturer, despite suffering a seven per cent drop in net profits to A$243 million for the 1996 calendar year. There are a number of serious problems looming fr the company's future profitability however, which include rising imports, an 11 per cent fall in national car sales this year, and a planned major capital expenditure program. Page 25.

Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd shareholders are today expected to approve the group's proposed acquisition of Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc. The deal will involve Coca-Cola Amatil issuing 293 million of its shares to San Miguel Corp and The Coca-Cola Co in exhange for their holdings in Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc. Page 26.

Australia's first corporate recovery fund was launched yesterday, with the initial focus being on plans to raise A$100 million from pension funds and institutional investors. The Corporate Recovery Fund will be managed by Corporate Recovery Partners Pty td, and headed by merchant banker Geoff Hill, and will be similar in set up to US funds known as "vulture" or "work out" funds. Page 26.

The Australian Institute of Company Directors (AICD) has urged the Federal Government to hold a comprehensive inquiry into the taxation system. AICD president John Ralph said yesterday that as the tax debate deteriorates into fruitless arguments over the merits of a goods and services tax, a major review of the system with input from all concerned parties is needed to establish areas which require reform. Page 32.

Australian mining company Resolute Ltd has reached an agreement with the Tanzanian Government which will allow it to develop large-scale gold mining projects in the resources rich East African country. Resolute's chief executive Michael Carrick said yesterday that the company could now begin operations at its Golden Pride mine, which would be a significant boost for Tanzania's infant mining industry. Page 32.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The meat industry is set to pressure individual Federal and State MPs in an attempt to persuade the Howard Government to abandon plans to double the export registration fees charged by the Australian Quarantine and Inspection Service (AQIS). The Government's move follows the decision to aim for full cost recovery in AQIS charges, and has been condemned by the industry, which claims it will lead to abattoir closures and significant job losses. Page 25.

BHP chief executive John Prescott said yesterday the company would have to undergo major changes if it was to meet new performance targets set for its 90 business units. Speaking at BHP's annual results and prospects seminar in Melbourne, Prescott exlained how the Australian resources company was in a transition period which will see operations divide into five performance categories, and a shift in emphasis from operational performance to long-term shareholder wealth creation. Page 25.

A New South Wales Supreme Court has rejected a A$158 million damages claim against Australis Media by Albert Hadid. Hadid claimed Australis backed out of a 1994 agreement to give him narrowcast channels in exchange for his withdrawal from bidding for six microwave licences. Page 25.

Australian company John B Fairfax's Rural Press has paid A$76.5 million for the Farm Progress Group, the biggest agricultural information provider in the US. Rural Press managing director Brian McCarthy said the acquisition would be used as a base for futher expansion into Northern hemisphere markets. page 25.

The founders of Australian-based cosmetics business Nutri-Metics International, Imelda and Bill Roche, have sold their company to US-based Sara Lee Corp for an undisclosed amount. Imelda Roche will remain as the company's chairman, while Bill Roche will be employed as a consultant and their eldest daughter Clare will take up the position of deputy chairman.

The directors of Hawker Richardson have reversed their earlier position and now say they will approve a takeover attempt by the Austrim group, following an improved offer from the investment company. Austrim yesterday proposed to pay A$1.86 a share, an inrease on the A$1.60 a share offered to Hawker shareholders last week, raising the company's value to A$67.8 million. Page 26.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

ANZ Bank chairman Charles Goode yesterday denied rumours that the surprise departure of chief executive Don Mercer had been provoked by conflict within the bank's board. Mercer's retirement was approved in March by ANZ's board but wasn't announced until late May, fuelling speculation that Mercer had opposed the management shake-up which forced the early retirement of three senior executives. Page 27.

Federal Budget changes which have significantly tightened access to locked-up superannuation benefits for members younger than 55 have caused a marked increase in requests to the superannuation industry regulatory body for early release of funds. Assistant commissioner Roger Brown said yesterday that the ISC had received over 6,000 applications in the past fortnight for early release of benefits, mainly for reasons of financial hardship or permanent relocation overseas. Page 29.

The Metal Trades Industry Association National Survey of Business Conditions has revealed that manufacturers are continuing to cut staff levels and experiencing weak levels of product demand. The manufacturing and small business sectors have not reportedany upturn in business conditions, despite four cuts in official interest rates over the past year. Page 29.

Federal Finance Minister John Fahey will today confirm that Macquarie Bank has secured the contract for the Federal Government's automotive fleet management company, DASfleet, and will pay A$410 million for the business. The Federal Government plans to use the sale's proceeds to improve the 1997-98 Federal Budget surplus. Page 29.

Committal hearings of insider trading charges will begin today against former Macquarie Bank executive Simon Hannes. The committal hearings were delayed yesterday because of a dispute over the confidentiality of documents supplied by the Australian Securties Commission. Page 29.

BHP Mineral's chief Dick Carter yesterday announced a gold deposit find in north-west Canada which the company believes will yield several million ounces. Carter confirmed that the find at Hope Bay was one of the biggest world-wide in recent years and wold boost BHP's efforts to become a leading player in the international gold industry. Page 30.
THE AGE

With debts of A$470,000 to 125 creditors, the Australian Marketing Institute has been placed in voluntary administration to Grant Thornton. The decision comes at a time when the organisation was positioning itself for a major role in the education of marketers in Australia. AMI has a current membership of 5500, up from 4400 last year. Page B1

New Zealand pet supply company Masterpet Corporation has paid approximately A$6 million for 50 per cent of leading independent Australian company Pets International. Masterpet dominates the pet supply market in New Zealand and hopes to achieve similar leels of dominance in Australia. Page B2.

BHP Petroleum's employees have benefited from the record profit the company recorded this financial year, which before abnormal items was A$693 million - up 66 per cent from the previous year. The 2400-strong workforce has been granted a bonus equal to 2 per cent of their annual gross salary. Page B2.

News Ltd has sold its half-share in Australian company Australian Newsprint Mill to New Zealand-based Fletcher Challenge FCLTP.NZ. The move was finalised yesterday in time for the end of the financial year, and will see Fletcher Challenge assume a A$60 million loan repayment owed to News Ltd by ANM. Page B3.

Australia's minor telecommunications companies have welcomed the advent of full deregulation, which takes place today, by offering a range of cheap call options to consumers. AAP Telecommunications has launched a residential long-distance phone service wich will undercut main rivals Telstra and Optus by up to 60 per cent. Page B3.

A move by electricity retailer CitiPower to cut its tariffs will result in the average business customer saving A$840 per year. CitiPower chairman Tom Wright said that since the company's establishment in 1994, some customers had received price cuts of up to 20 per cent in real terms. Page B2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
